<command-name>/mise:next</command-name>
<command-args>Extraction provenance and file-level notes in the diff
Goal
Let the cluster skill declare that a file was extracted from a region of another file, and let the reviewer see that provenance inside the diff: a note pinned to the top of the diff editor, and a left side that shows only the extracted region instead of the whole origin file. Also allow a free-text one-liner per file, for any file, shown in the same places.

Contract changes (clusters file, version 3)
Bump version to 3. The extension accepts 1, 2, and 3. The skill writes 3.
moves[].fromLines — optional. Array of [start, end] pairs, 1-based inclusive line numbers into the origin file as it stood at the merge base. Non-empty, ascending, non-overlapping. Only meaningful on origin: "repo". Silently dropped on an external entry, the same way donor is dropped on a repo entry.
moves[].baseBlob — now also meaningful on origin: "repo". It names the blob holding the extracted content: the declared lines concatenated in order. On external entries it keeps its current meaning, the whole donor file. One concept in both cases: the content the file came from.
notes — optional top-level object mapping a repo-relative file path to a one-line string. Any file in the review set may have one. Entries for files outside the review set are silently ignored.
Malformed shapes reject the whole file, per the existing rule. Semantic misses, such as lines past the end of the origin, degrade at runtime rather than at parse time.
Update plugin/skills/cluster/SKILL.md Contract and DEVELOPMENT.md in the same commit as the parser.
Extension: sliced origin diff
For a repo move with fromLines, read the origin's merge-base blob, cut the declared lines, and write the slice to the object store with hash-object -w --stdin. Its sha becomes the diff base sha. The diff base path stays the origin path, as it does today for repo moves.
Resolution order for a repo move, after the existing snapshot and own-merge-base precedence:
Slice sha equals baseBlob, or no baseBlob was declared: use the slice.
Mismatch and baseBlob is readable: search the merge-base origin text for the blob's content. First exact match wins. Found: use it, and display the re-derived lines. Not found: use baseBlob directly as the base and drop the line pointer from labels.
Lines out of range and no usable baseBlob: fall back to the whole origin file, with a warning line in the tooltip and thread.
A readable baseBlob also rescues a repo move whose origin path no longer exists at the merge base, which today shows an empty left side.
Verbatim fires when the working-tree sha equals the resolved origin base sha, so an extraction that is exactly the slice reads as verbatim.
Anchor every slice blob the extension writes on a review-owned ref so gc cannot prune it, following the pattern in src/reviewState.ts and src/notesStore.ts. A skill-written baseBlob with the same content is covered by the same anchor.
Cache the slice sha per origin blob sha plus lines, so a refresh does not rehash unchanged input.
The origin file keeps its own row as a normal modification. The existing suppression applies only when the origin was deleted from the working tree.
Base-side review notes keep working unchanged. They locate by snapshot text and content blob, not by line number, so a slice document needs no special casing.
Extension: file-level provenance thread
One comment thread pinned to the top of the diff, created with range set to undefined so it is a file-level thread. Shown on the document the diff's right side displays.
Body, in order, only the parts that exist: the origin line, the move note, the per-file note. Example: "Extracted from src/old/big.ts lines 120-180. Swapped its logger for ours."
Read-only: no reply box, no edit or delete actions, never written to the notes contract, never listed in the Review Notes view, never counted as a review note anywhere.
Rebuilt on every model refresh. Removed when the file has nothing to show.
Expanded by default.
Carries the fallback warning when the slice could not be resolved.
Extension: tree view and titles
Row suffix appends the line range to the origin: ← big.ts:120-180 · verbatim. Multiple ranges compact to the first plus an ellipsis; the tooltip lists all of them. Existing shortening rules still apply.
Tooltip gains the per-file note as its own line, after the move note.
Diff title reads "extracted from src/old/big.ts:120-180" when lines resolved, "moved from" otherwise.
Cluster skill
Declare fromLines and baseBlob only for an extraction the agent performed in the invoking task or the user described. Never inferred from the diff.
Compute the blob from the merge base, not the working tree:

git show "$MERGE_BASE:src/old/big.ts" | sed -n '120,180p' | git hash-object -w --stdin
Multiple ranges concatenate in order before hashing.
On every re-run, for each preserved repo move that has fromLines: re-slice at the current merge base and hash. Match: keep. Mismatch: search the current origin for the baseBlob content and rewrite fromLines to where it now sits. Not found: drop fromLines, keep baseBlob. This relocates declared content and does not count as inferring provenance.
Write a notes entry when a file warrants a one-liner for the reviewer. Preserve existing entries on re-runs the way moves are preserved. Drop entries whose file left the review set.
Report declared extractions and notes alongside clusters and moves in the final summary.
Edge cases already decided
Destination existed at the merge base: its own merge-base blob stays the diff base, per today's rule. The slice is used only for the verbatim or adapted classification.
Reviewed snapshot base: wins over everything, as today.
Several files extracted from one origin: each is its own move entry with its own lines. The base-document resolution in src/baseDocument.ts already handles two review files sharing a base path.
Both moves[].note and notes[path] present for one file: show both, move note first.
A move with baseBlob but no fromLines on a repo origin: valid. The blob is the base, no line pointer shown.
Rebase where upstream edited the extracted block itself: the blob is not found in the new origin, so the diff runs against the blob and the label loses its line pointer. The next skill run does not restore lines, because there is nothing to relocate to.
Out of scope
Auto-detecting extractions by content matching. The contract forbids inferred provenance.
More than one origin file per destination.
Editable or reply-capable provenance threads.
Character-level ranges. Lines only.
Verification
Unit tests for the parser, slice resolution and fallback chain, the row and tooltip text, and the thread body composition, all kept free of VS Code imports.
One scripted extension-host check per the DEVELOPMENT.md recipe that opens a diff for a declared extraction and confirms the file-level thread renders above line 1 and the left document is the slice. Batch it with any other extension-host launches.
Manual test script in DEVELOPMENT.md gains steps for a declared extraction, a rebase that shifts lines, and a per-file note.
Release
Extension minor bump and plugin version bump in the same release, since both sides of the contract change.</command-args>

**Keepalive caller for callables**

Problem: when a tap sends the page away (for example a WhatsApp link), the browser cancels a callable request that is still in flight. `httpsCallable` offers no way to set `keepalive`, so apps end up building the callable request by hand, and that copy breaks silently if the region or emulator setup changes.

Ask: a fire-and-forget caller, for example `createKeepaliveCaller(functions, name)`, that:

Sends a callable protocol request with `fetch(..., { keepalive: true })`.
Builds the URL from the `Functions` instance the way `httpsCallable` does: region, custom domain, and emulator host and port.
Gets the App Check token, and the auth token when someone is signed in, before sending, since nothing can wait once the page starts to leave.
Skips connectivity handling and rate limiting, and never throws. Failures go to an optional `onError` callback.
Respects the `keepalive` body limit of 64 KB.</command-args>

<command-args>The following is a report from a project that consumes this package. Take it with a grain of salt. Investigate the code and potential usage issues and before continuing tell me your thoughts and wheter this is an actual bug or the consumer is using it wrong.
---
Bug: getDocWithCache cannot recover from a getsetdel store reset — its three retries always fail

Version: firebase-kit-client 3.0.0, getsetdel as bundled.

What happened
A Nuxt page (Okven /staff/dashboard?tab=sources) fanned out several db.getDocWithCache reads on the businesses store while another tab on the same origin cleared Private-tagged stores (clear(token) → inventory entry deleted). Every read then threw Error('Failed to read through cache after 3 attempts') after ~7 s (1 + 2 + 4 s backoff) and the app fell to its fatal error page. Reproduced deterministically by triggering a reset between createStore and the first cache read; each of getsetdel's three reset reasons (store was deleted, creation time mismatch, version mismatch) produces the same outcome.

Root cause
firestore/internal/getDocWithCache.js calls createStore(...) once, before readThroughCache, and closes over that token in readCache/writeCache/dropCache. readThroughCache.js catches GetSetDelResetError, backs off, and retries the same closures — with the same stale token. getsetdel's checkStoreState compares the token's creation/version/tags against the inventory on every call, so once the inventory has changed the token can never pass again. The retry loop is unreachable success for this error class.

getDocsWithCache.js does it right: it calls createStore inside its attempt loop, so a retry reads the fresh inventory and gets a new token.

Proposed fix
Mirror getDocsWithCache: move createStore into the attempt, i.e. have readThroughCache accept a factory (openStore: () => Promise<StoreToken>) called at the top of each attempt, or re-create the token in getDocWithCache per attempt and pass the closures fresh. Keep the GetSetDelResetError-only retry filter and the backoff.

Test to add
In readThroughCache/getDocWithCache tests: create the store, simulate a reset with getsetdel's simulateStoreReset(token) (or delete the inventory entry) before the first read, and assert the read succeeds on the second attempt with a fresh token rather than throwing after three. A second case: reset landing between readCache and writeCache.

Related but separate (host side)
The host's logged-out cleanup ran on the standing state loaded && !isLoggedIn, so a never-logged-in tab kept clearing Private stores for other tabs. That is the host's bug, but the library should still survive a reset from any tab, since IndexedDB is shared across them.

Also worth considering
subscribeWithCache.js uses the same pattern; check whether its token is refreshed on reconnect.</command-args>
